A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FairICP by the same authors, with matching algorithms and substantial shared experiments. All pages, including appendices, are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: V3 reports original permutation-quality simulations, fairness–accuracy experiments, and evaluations on Communities and Crime, Adult, and COMPAS, including appendix results.

after.justification: V4 reports original simulations and real-data evaluations, including added ACSIncome results and expanded classification comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Equations (2)–(7) and Algorithms 1–3 retain the adversarial objective, inverse conditional permutation distribution, alternating training, fairness test, and pairwise sampler. Additional estimator specifications document implementations without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds ACSIncome classification with jointly protected sex, race, and continuous age, providing a mixed-type sensitive-attribute setting absent from v3's evaluations. The downstream learning simulations also replace independently generated sensitive attributes with correlated mixtures; the earlier permutation-quality experiment already used correlation.

E2.justification: GerryFair is newly evaluated on ACSIncome, Adult, and COMPAS. FDL joins the Adult and COMPAS comparisons for both neural and linear predictors, whereas v3 evaluated it only on Crimes among the real datasets. The simulation comparator set remains FairICP, FairCP, FDL, and Oracle.

E3.justification: V4 adds DEO evaluation for Adult and COMPAS. Appendix E.2 also revises reported training searches: FairICP classification epochs change from a 50–300 grid to a 20–200 grid, batch-size and discriminator learning-rate choices change, fairness-penalty grids expand, and HGR activation changes from ReLU to SeLU. These are reported setting changes, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: The resampling ablations and dimension/dependence sensitivity experiments in Figures 3 and 6 are revised for correlated sensitive attributes. V4 additionally checks sensitivity to the fairness metric through DEO trade-off analyses on Adult and COMPAS, including linear predictors. The earlier permutation-quality analyses using linear and MAF density estimation are retained.

E5.justification: V4 Table 2 specifies that runtime means average five trials; v3 Table 1 gives mean runtimes without a separate timing repetition count. The existing 20-trial permutation studies, 100-run or split evaluations, and prediction-loss standard deviations remain. This establishes new reporting, not an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: V4 adds ACSIncome, comparator, and DEO results and replaces numerous simulation and classification curves. In Table 1, Adult's unfair-baseline KPC/power changes from 0.020/0.06 to 0.042/0.93; the FairICP COMPAS loss/KPC point changes from 0.352/0.031 to 0.402/0.008. Changed simulation distributions and tuning settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: V4 removes Theorem 2.1's converse and asymptotic fairness result under log(p)/n tending to zero, along with Theorem 2.4's optimal-and-fair predictor guarantee and their proofs. The revised theorem promotes the existing conditional-permutation identity and retains the forward implication under equalized odds. Testing validity survives as Proposition 2.2. New Appendix A derives a special-case relationship between KPC and squared partial correlation.

C1.justification: V3's explicit Theoretical Guarantees contribution, asserting asymptotic equalized odds, disappears from v4's introduction. The method's guarantee is narrowed to distributional equality when equalized odds already holds. The real-data claim also changes from best performance across all tasks to most tasks, while the central ICP proposal and empirical trade-off claim remain.

C2.justification: V4 removes Remark 2.2's explicit finite-sample non-equivalence warning and one-observation example, as well as the COMPAS-specific intrinsic-bias qualification. It expands interpretation of KPC and density-estimation advantages, discusses possible post-processing applications, and explicitly identifies access to sensitive attributes during training as a deployment constraint.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly specifies MAF architectures and optimization for simulations and real data, the classification density estimator, losses, and detailed GerryFair and Reduction configurations. It also adds links identifying baseline source implementations. These substantially improve implementation documentation without establishing that every newly described setting changed.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including Cho, Ding, Gretton, Madras, and Tifrea, with new discussion of post-processing and GerryFair's relationship to equalized odds. Bao and Naaman are removed, and Scott's 1991 article is replaced by a different 2015 book. The central positioning around complex sensitive attributes remains.

P1.justification: The title changes to FairICP: Encouraging Equalized Odds via Inverse Conditional Permutation. V4 edits and expands explanatory passages, groups downstream simulations under Section 3.1.2, and reorganizes appendix subsections. Much wording and the Introduction–Method–Experiments–Discussion narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout. Simulation panels are rearranged, Table 1 gains dataset/comparator/DEO columns while runtimes move to appendix Table 2, and new ACSIncome and DEO plots appear. Existing classification figures also gain comparator curves and metric panels.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens empirical support for the central mixed-attribute use case through ACSIncome, fuller classification comparisons, and DEO checks, while Appendix E substantially improves reproducibility information. The net gain is tempered by the loss of asymptotic/optimality analyses and the explicit finite-sample caveat, although the corresponding headline guarantees are also narrowed.
